main_text.p: caufis.Morborum totius substantiae (inqt) alij quidem manifesti sunt, alij occulti. Manifesti ut scabies, phthisis, horumque simi-les. Et libro de Externis affectibus, cap.5. ipsam scabiem esse affectum ex intemperie calida, dissolutione continui, compositum his verbis indicat. Scabies alpredo cutis est, seu leuis exulceratio pruriens, aut interdum rodens. Fit aut ex humidiore qua-vis pustula, sive pallida, sive livida, sive nigra fit: quae rupta ulcusculum in cute profert humidum, aut etiam interdum expur-gata sanie aridum, idq; modo cum pruri-gine sola, modo cum leui rubore in ambi-tu, cumq; calore, ac dolore. Ex reficcata sa-nie crustula obdurescit, qua saepe ulcusculum obducitur. Haec Fernelius, quibus sibi dissentire satis arguit. Nam morbus, quem totius substantiae statuit, & continui dissolutio-plurimum inter se discrepant: quandoquidem ille partis similaris dutaxat est vitium. Haec vero tum similarium, tum dissimilarium partium communis morbus, quem admodum aperte docet ipse Fernelius, capite nono lib. de Morborum differentiis, ubi de communi morbo expresse tractat.

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "cutis" after "alpredo" (partly obscured by a stain/mark on the scan) and the word after "quauis" are read from the scan with some uncertainty. Printing irregularities kept as printed: "diffentire" for dissentire is normalised to "dissentire" by the long-s rule; "dissolutio-plurimum" has a dash where a full stop/semicolon may be intended. The "»" marks at line ends are printed ornaments, not text. The "Ma-nifesti" break appears without a printed hyphen and is written whole.
